Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Κικιλία, Βαλεριανός και Τιβούρτιος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the title on the name link behind her clause for 22 ноября ст. ст., name page 2551, «Кикилия (Цецилия) Римская, мц.», with the rank word left off. The parenthesis is the source’s own: the day line prints the same pair, «Мц. Кикилии (Цецилии)», and the calendar offers no third reading to settle which of the two is the lemma. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 22. новембар ст. ст., „Св. мученица Кикилија (Цицилија).“ — «Св.» is “saint” and «мученица» is the `martyr` grade `types` already keeps, so both come off. THE HEADING PRINTS TWO SPELLINGS AND ONLY ONE IS STORED: «Кикилија» is the heading's own form and «(Цицилија)» is an alternative beside it, not a second word of the name, and §6 allows one form per folder — storing the pair would key as the two-word string «кикилија цицилија», which is neither spelling. The variant is recorded here instead. Measured: no other folder in the corpus holds either string.

attestations.note: The life page `https://www.saint.gr/3059/saint.aspx` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the woman is the folder's own: the noble girl of the third century baptised against her idolatrous parents' religion, married to Valerian, beheaded in the persecution under Diocletian. The page's line enumerates two more by name, Valerian and Tiburtius, and both are new folders in this day's batch; the same day keeps `maximus-the-capitularius`, who the page says believed through her and Valerian. A death interval is proposed from the reign the page names, where the folder had none. Both hymns name her and no other saint and both carry an ἦχος and a model: the Ἀπολυτίκιον also calls the two men «τὴν αὐτάδελφον δυάδα καὶ σύναυλον» and is drafted onto their folders too, and the Κοντάκιον, which names the prefect Almachius, is hers alone. The page's Οἶκος is neither a troparion nor a kontakion and is not drafted. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 05.12.2025 (22. новембар ст. ст.) — „Св. мученица Кикилија (Цицилија).“

attestations.note: The day's first entry. `dates` UNTOUCHED: the book says «Пострада св. Кикилија са осталима око 230. год.», about 230, which is the earlier of the two readings this folder already holds as «230 or under Diocletian (284–305)» — a year inside an interval the corpus deliberately refused to choose between, so a third book agreeing with one side of it does not close it. No `related` row added: Valerian, Tiburtius and Maximus the guard are all three related both ways already, and the bishop Urban the entry names is identified with none of the five Urbans the corpus keeps, none of whom is a bishop of Rome. WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS: rich and notable parents at Rome, the lifelong vow of virginity and the rough hair shirt worn under the costly clothes her parents gave her, the counsel to the bridegroom on the first night to go to bishop Urban and be baptised and then live a virgin life himself, Valerian converting his own brother, the two brothers winning the captain of the guard on the way to execution and all three suffering together, Cecilia burying their bodies together, FOUR HUNDRED SOULS WON IN ONE EVENING, her answer to the judge that her boldness came «од чисте савести и од вере несумњиве» — of a clean conscience and a faith without doubt — the executioner striking her neck three times without killing her, the faithful gathering the blood from the wound in kerchiefs, sponges and vessels for healing, the three days before she gave up her spirit, her relics resting in the church of her name at Rome, and that the western church counts her the patroness of church singing and music. Measured: no other folder holds «Кикилија».

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Cecilia, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un Milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mucenițe Cecilia (the common «Mielușeaua Ta», with her name set into it)

english.text: Your ewe-lamb Cecilia cries out to you with a loud voice, O Jesus: you, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking you I suffer; with you I am crucified and with you buried in your baptism; and I suffer for your sake, that I may reign in you; and I die for you, that I may live for you. Receive me, then, as a spotless sacrifice, offered to you in love. At her prayers, as you are merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Θείων τρόπων σου, τὴ ἐπιλάμψει, πρὸς ἀείζωον, εἴλκυσας φέγγος, τὴν αὐτάδελφον δυάδα καὶ σύναυλον καὶ σὺν αὐτοὶς Κικιλία ἀθλήσασα, τῆς θείας δόξης ὁμοῦ ἠξιώθητε. Μεθ' ὧν πρέσβευε, δοθήναι τοὶς εὐφημούσι σέ, πταισμάτων ἱλασμὸν καὶ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιοι Κικιλία, Βαλεριανός και Τιβούρτιος». It names her and calls the two men «τὴν αὐτάδελφον δυάδα καὶ σύναυλον», the pair of brothers who shared her house, and names no other saint. The readings «τὴ», «αὐτοὶς», «δοθήναι» and «τοὶς» are the page's own and are copied as they stand.

english.text: By the shining of your godly ways you drew to the ever-living light the pair of brothers who shared your house; and contending with them, Cecilia, you were all together counted worthy of the divine glory. With them, intercede that forgiveness of offences and great mercy be given to those who praise you.

hymns.text: Τὴν νυμφευθεῖσαν, τῷ Χριστῷ ἑκουσίως, καὶ στολισθεῖσαν, ἀρεταῖς τὴν καρδίαν, θεοπρεπῶς ὑμνήσωμεν Πιστῶν ἡ πληθύς· αὕτη γὰρ κατήσχυνεν, Ἀλμακίου τὸ θράσος, λάμψασα ὡς ἥλιος, μέσον τῶν ἐκζητούντων, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὤφθη τοῖς ἐν γῇ, στήριγμα θεῖον, τὴν πίστιν κρατύνασα.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ὁ ὑψωθεὶς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ — on the page of «Άγιοι Κικιλία, Βαλεριανός και Τιβούρτιος». It speaks of her alone, names no other saint, and names the prefect Almachius, whom the page's own narrative does not.

english.text: Let us, the multitude of the faithful, sing as befits God of her who was wedded to Christ by her own will and whose heart was arrayed in the virtues; for she put the insolence of Almachius to shame, shining like the sun in the midst of those who sought her out, and afterwards was shown to those on earth a divine support, having made the faith strong.

death.note: Two calendars disagree and the corpus chooses neither. saint.gr set the three under Diocletian, «Κατά τον επί Διοκλητιανού διωγμόν», which is 284–305; the Russian calendar’s day line closes the clause «(ок. 230)» and its life page kills Maximus, the last of the four, at «(+ 230)». The interval carries both readings and the basis stays traditional, as it was on the Greek reading alone.
